answer: Each identity anchors its work to one crystal source for a 75-credit bond and 15 fee. The ledger caps each crystal source at a summit of 40 claims per epoch; each identity posts a plume record of its uses. Auditors count a source's plume records against its cap: claims past 40 void and every tied identity loses its bond. The k-th fake pays 90 and risks burning earlier fakes sharing its crystal, so 1,000 fakes cost 90,000. A rented-source ring fails: the crystal receipt is key-bound, duplicate plume entries rejected. An honest agent pays 90 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
